data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes policy and defines roles and responsibilities for conducting United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Computer Matching Programs (CMPs).
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Computer Matching Programs (CMPs)

policy_statements.source_text: This DR also addresses the use of computerized comparisons of two or more automated information systems for establishing and verifying Federal benefit program eligibility or recouping payments, delinquent debts, or overpayments owed to Government Agencies from a Federal benefit program.
policy_statements.target: use of computerized comparisons of two or more automated information systems

policy_statements.source_text: This DR supersedes DR 3450-001, Computer Matching Projects Involving Individual Privacy Data, dated April 17, 1984.
cross_references: DR 3450-001, Computer Matching Projects Involving Individual Privacy Data

policy_statements.source_text: This policy is effective immediately and remains in effect until it is superseded or expires.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their policies and procedures with this policy within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: The terms “regulation” and “policy” may be used interchangeably.
The Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act of 1988, Public Law (P.L.) 100-503, will be commonly referred to in this document as the Computer Matching Act.
cross_references: Computer Matching and Privacy Protection Act of 1988, Public Law (P.L.) 100-503
Computer Matching Act

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all:
USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, field offices, and program offices;
USDA employees, contractors, interns, partners, volunteers, and affiliates working for, or on behalf of, USDA;
conditions: working for, or on behalf of, USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Automated information systems or services (including cloud-based services) used or operated by, for, or on behalf of USDA, including interconnections between or among these systems or services; and
conditions: used or operated by, for, or on behalf of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Facilities from which these systems or services operate whether owned or operated by USDA or owned or operated on behalf of USDA by a contractor, subcontractor, or other organization.
The USDA is committed to preserving and enhancing privacy protections for all individuals, promoting transparency of USDA operations, and serving as a leader in the Federal privacy community.
The CMP uses a Computer Matching Agreement (CMA) to fulfill this commitment.

A CMA is a written agreement that establishes the conditions, safeguards, and procedures under which a Federal organization agrees to disclose data where there is a computerized comparison of two or more automated system of records (SOR).

The Computer Matching Act amended the Privacy Act of 1974, 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 552a, and establishes procedural safeguards affecting Agencies’ use of Privacy Act SOR while using certain types of CMPs.
cross_references: Computer Matching Act
Privacy Act of 1974, 5 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 552a
Privacy Act

policy_statements.source_text: The Computer Matching Act regulates the use of computer matching by Federal Agencies involving personally identifiable records maintained in a SOR subject to the Privacy Act.
cross_references: Computer Matching Act
Privacy Act

policy_statements.source_text: The Computer Matching Act requires Agencies to have written agreements in place specifying the terms under which matches are to be conducted and by adding certain protections for individuals applying for and receiving Federal benefits.
cross_references: Computer Matching Act

policy_statements.source_text: The Computer Matching Act applies to the computerized comparison of two or more automated SORs (or Federal personnel or payroll SORs) between Federal Agencies or between a Federal Agency and a non-Federal Agency.
cross_references: Computer Matching Act

policy_statements.source_text: The Computer Matching Act covers two kinds of matching programs:
cross_references: Computer Matching Act

policy_statements.source_text: Matching that involves establishing or verifying eligibility or compliance with laws and regulations by applicants for recipients and beneficiaries with respect to, cash, in-kind assistance or payments under Federal benefit programs; or recouping payments or delinquent debts under such Federal benefit programs; and
Program matches using records from Federal personnel or payroll SOR relating to Federal personnel management.
USDA’s CMA procedures are defined in the USDA OCIO’s Information Security Center (ISC), Computer Matching Agreement: Standard Operating Procedure.
cross_references: USDA OCIO’s Information Security Center (ISC), Computer Matching Agreement: Standard Operating Procedure

policy_statements.source_text: The Improper Payments Elimination and Recovery Improvement Act of 2012 (IPERIA), P.L. 112-248, was designed to provide guidance to help Federal Agencies protect privacy while improving the oversight of payments to prevent waste, fraud, and abuse in Federal spending.
cross_references: Improper Payments Elimination and Recovery Improvement Act of 2012 (IPERIA), P.L. 112-248

policy_statements.source_text: The Do Not Pay (DNP) Initiative introduced by Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-13-20, Protecting Privacy while Reducing Improper Payments with the Do Not Pay Initiative, implements Section 5 of IPERIA.
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-13-20, Protecting Privacy while Reducing Improper Payments with the Do Not Pay Initiative
Section 5 of IPERIA

policy_statements.source_text: IPERIA establishes standards and procedures that apply to matching programs conducted exclusively for purposes of the DNP Initiative.
cross_references: IPERIA

policy_statements.source_text: OMB Circular A-108, Federal Agency Responsibilities for Review, Reporting, and Publication under the Privacy Act, supplements and clarifies existing OMB guidance, including OMB Circular A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource, and the Privacy Act.
cross_references: OMB Circular A-108, Federal Agency Responsibilities for Review, Reporting, and Publication under the Privacy Act
OMB Circular A-130, Managing Information as a Strategic Resource
Privacy Act

policy_statements.source_text: Specifically, OMB Circular A-108 Section 8, Publishing Matching Notices; Section 9, Reporting Matching Programs to OMB and Congress; Appendix V – Full Notice of Federal Register Matching Notice Template; and Appendix VI – Revision Notice of Federal Register Matching Notice Template, capture the mechanics of the CMP in a condensed version and are also addressed in the USDA OCIO’s ISC, Computer Matching Agreement: Standard Operating Procedure.
cross_references: OMB Circular A-108 Section 8, Publishing Matching Notices; Section 9, Reporting Matching Programs to OMB and Congress; Appendix V – Full Notice of Federal Register Matching Notice Template; and Appendix VI – Revision Notice of Federal Register Matching Notice Template
USDA OCIO’s ISC, Computer Matching Agreement: Standard Operating Procedure

policy_statements.source_text: USDA will:
Comply with the Computer Matching Act;
cross_references: Computer Matching Act

policy_statements.source_text: Establish CMPs when conducting matching of two or more personally identifiable information (PII) records or SORs, as a computerized comparison of SORs for establishing or verifying eligibility or recouping payments for a Federal benefit program, or relating to Federal personnel management.
conditions: when conducting matching of two or more personally identifiable information (PII) records or SORs, as a computerized comparison of SORs for establishing or verifying eligibility or recouping payments for a Federal benefit program, or relating to Federal personnel management

policy_statements.source_text: Matching entities may be Federal, state, or local government agencies, as well as contractors for such agencies;
Ensure the Department establishes an internal Data Integrity Board (DIB) to oversee and approve use of CMPs and cost benefit analyses (CBA).
The DIB should be composed of senior officials designated by the USDA Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP);

policy_statements.source_text: Evaluate and determine if CMPs meets DNP Initiative requirements;
Ensure the Privacy Act matching program for the DNP Initiative is termed “Do Not Pay matching program” when matching with at least one of these databases:
conditions: when matching with at least one of these databases
cross_references: Privacy Act

cross_references: Section 5(b)(1)(B) of IPERIA

policy_statements.source_text: The DNP matching programs have alternative standards and procedures as provided in M-13-20 and the USDA OCIO ISC, Computer Matching Agreement: Standard Operating Procedure.
cross_references: USDA OCIO ISC, Computer Matching Agreement: Standard Operating Procedure

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) will:
Serve as the USDA SAOP;
Provide executive leadership and overall management for the Department’s Privacy Program;
Allocate resources to implement and operate the Departmental Privacy Program;
Review, approve, and implement USDA’s CMP policy;
Sign transmittal letters for a new or modified matching program.
Review, approve, and maintain a list of the systems across the Department that process or collect PII;
policy_statements.target: list of the systems across the Department that process or collect PII

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that Federal statutory and regulatory requirements, guidelines, Departmental directives, and other applicable guidance are met.
Chair the DIB; and
Designate the Department’s senior agency officials who will comprise the DIB;
The DIB will:
At a minimum, consist of the USDA SAOP and the Inspector General or their designee.
policy_statements.target: USDA SAOP and the Inspector General or their designee

policy_statements.source_text: Additional members may include any senior officials designated by the SAOP, to include the USDA Chief Privacy Officer (CPO), who serves as the DIB Secretary.
Oversee and coordinate the implementation of the Privacy Act as it relates to the Department’s participation in matching programs;
cross_references: Privacy Act

policy_statements.source_text: Review, approve, and maintain all Departmental CMAs;
Annually review each ongoing matching program in which the Department has participated during the year to:
Ensure that the statutory and regulatory requirements, OMB guidelines, and Departmental policies have been met;
policy_statements.target: statutory and regulatory requirements, OMB guidelines, and Departmental policies

policy_statements.source_text: Assess the costs and benefits of the matching program; and
policy_statements.target: costs and benefits of the matching program

policy_statements.source_text: Determine if the matching program should be continued.
Review the Department’s record-keeping and disposal policies and practices for matching programs to ensure compliance with applicable record retention requirements delineated in:
DR 3080-001, Records Management;
cross_references: DR 3080-001, Records Management

policy_statements.source_text: DR 3085-001, Vital Records Management Program;
cross_references: DR 3085-001, Vital Records Management Program

policy_statements.source_text: Provide interpretation and guidance to the Department’s staff on the requirements for matching programs;
Serve as the Department’s clearinghouse to:
Receive and release information on the accuracy, completeness, and reliability of records used in matching programs;

policy_statements.source_text: Report CMAs to Congress and OMB; and
Submit an annual report on matching activities to the Secretary and to OMB;
The DIB may also review and report on any Departmental matching activities that are not defined as matching programs under the Computer Matching Act.
conditions: that are not defined as matching programs under the Computer Matching Act

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the contact for privacy policies, procedures, and CMAs;
Prepare and draft the CMA overview summary presentation to include in the CMP package;
Develop, establish, and ensure compliance with Departmental policies and procedures regarding Computer Matching Act administration;
policy_statements.target: Departmental policies and procedures regarding Computer Matching Act administration
cross_references: Computer Matching Act

policy_statements.source_text: Review new CMAs, 12-month extension renewals of existing matching programs, CBA, new or altered matching program notices, and new or altered matching program reports prior to submission to the Department’s DIB;
policy_statements.target: new CMAs, 12-month extension renewals of existing matching programs, CBA, new or altered matching program notices, and new or altered matching program reports

policy_statements.source_text: Prepare an annual report to the USDA Secretary and OMB on current matching agreements;
Ensure the Department’s DIB transmits any new or altered matching program reports to OMB and Congress;
Ensure Notice of Computer Matching Program is transmitted to the Federal Register (FR) in accordance with Computer Matching Act;

Computer Matching Act

policy_statements.source_text: Provide technical assistance to system and program managers, as needed, in the development of the documentation required for CMAs; and
Establish and maintain a list of CMAs, to include effective dates and expirations.
The USDA Chief Information Security Officer will:
Review and approve new CMAs, 12-month renewals of existing matching programs, or altered matching program reports prior to submission to the Department’s DIB; and
policy_statements.target: new CMAs, 12-month renewals of existing matching programs, or altered matching program reports
conditions: prior to submission to the Department’s DIB

policy_statements.source_text: Provide the Departmental DIB with an Information Technology (IT) security assessment of the CMA and any associated cybersecurity risks.
Mission Area Assistant CIOs will:
Ensure all personnel are familiar with, and adhere to, the provisions of the CMA, this computer matching DR, and other applicable Departmental policies and procedures;
Ensure that a CMA is submitted by USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, field offices, and program offices participating in CMP, as defined in the Computer Matching Act.
cross_references: Computer Matching Act

policy_statements.source_text: At USDA, a CMA is also required for “pilot” program matches.

Pilot program matches usually last less than 6 months, using the smallest possible sampling of data, or access to data, deemed necessary to test and validate the efficacy of the program being considered.
No adverse actions will be taken against an individual whom PII is being matched, based on the results of a pilot program match including stop payments or awards actions;
Ensure all CMPs are submitted to the USDA CPO for DIB approval;
Provide the CPO with periodic updates (yearly at a minimum) on agency CMPs.

Updates, at a minimum, should include title, the Mission Area, agency, or staff office involved in the computer match, DIB approval, FR CMP announcement, computer match commencement, and computer match expiration date; and
Report to OMB and Congress any proposal to establish, re-establish, or modify a CMP that would change the purpose, defined elements, matching entities, or change PII variables per Circular A-108.
conditions: that would change the purpose, defined elements, matching entities, or change PII variables per Circular A-108
cross_references: Circular A-108

The USDA is committed to preserving and enhancing privacy protections for all individuals, promoting transparency of USDA operations, and serving as a leader in the Federal privacy community.
The CMP uses a Computer Matching Agreement (CMA) to fulfill this commitment.

A CMA is a written agreement that establishes the conditions, safeguards, and procedures under which a Federal organization agrees to disclose data where there is a computerized comparison of two or more automated system of records (SOR).

b. The *Computer Matching Act* amended the *Privacy Act of 1974*,  5 United States Code (U.S.C.) Section 552a , and establishes procedural safeguards affecting Agencies’ use of *Privacy Act* SOR while using certain types of CMPs. The *Computer Matching Act* regulates the use of computer matching by Federal Agencies involving personally identifiable records maintained in a SOR subject to the *Privacy Act*. The *Computer Matching Act* requires Agencies to have written agreements in place specifying the terms under which matches are to be conducted and by adding certain protections for individuals applying for and receiving Federal benefits. The *Computer Matching Act* applies to the computerized comparison of two or more automated SORs (or Federal personnel or payroll SORs) between Federal Agencies or between a Federal Agency and

The *Computer Matching Act* requires Agencies to have written agreements in place specifying the terms under which matches are to be conducted and by adding certain protections for individuals applying for and receiving Federal benefits
The *Computer Matching Act* covers two kinds of matching programs

Matching that involves establishing or verifying eligibility or compliance with laws and regulations by applicants for recipients and beneficiaries with respect to, cash, in-kind assistance or payments under Federal benefit programs; or recouping payments or delinquent debts under such Federal benefit programs; and
Program matches using records from Federal personnel or payroll SOR relating to Federal personnel management.

The *Improper Payments Elimination and Recovery Improvement Act of 2012* (IPERIA),  P.L. 112-248 , was designed to provide guidance to help Federal Agencies protect privacy while improving the oversight of payments to prevent waste, fraud, and abuse in Federal spending. The Do Not Pay (DNP) Initiative introduced by Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum  M-13-20 , *Protecting Privacy while Reducing Improper Payments with the Do Not Pay Initiative*, implements Section 5 of IPERIA. IPERIA establishes standards and procedures that apply to matching programs conducted exclusively for purposes of the DNP Initiative.

This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes policy and defines roles and responsibilities for conducting United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Computer Matching Programs (CMPs). This DR also addresses the use of computerized comparisons of two or more automated information systems for establishing and verifying Federal benefit program eligibility or recouping payments, delinquent debts, or overpayments owed to Government Agencies from a Federal benefit program.
d. Facilities from which these systems or services operate whether owned or operated by USDA or owned or operated on behalf of USDA by a contractor, subcontractor, or other organization.
